Summary table for HDX-MS reporting (Masson et al. 2019)

Source: R/reporting.R
hdx_summary_table.Rd

Builds the summary table recommended by Masson et al. (2019, Nat Methods 16:595) for publishing HDX-MS data: one row per item, one column per protein state. Items computed from the data: time course, controls, replicates, number of peptides, sequence coverage, average peptide length, redundancy, back-exchange (mean and range), repeatability (pooled replicate SD, Da) and the significance threshold: the critical interval used when each state is compared with the first state (the same values as in hdx_results_table()). Items that only you know (labeling buffer, pH, temperature, quench, protease, LC/MS, software ...) are added from metadata.

Usage

hdx_summary_table(
  filepath,
  metadata = list(),
  replicates = NULL,
  Dfact = 0.85,
  alpha = 0.01,
  pvalue = 0.01,
  protein_range = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  states = NULL
)

Arguments

filepath

input file or table, as for output_tp().

metadata

named list of extra items, e.g. list("HDX reaction details" = "20 mM HEPES pD 7.4, 90% D2O, 20 C"). A single value applies to every state; a vector gives one value per state. They are listed first.

replicates

optional maximum number of replicates per state. Default NULL uses every replicate.

Dfact

D2O fraction of the labeling buffer for back-exchange. Default 0.85.

alpha

alpha of the critical interval. Default 0.01.

pvalue

p-value cutoff, reported with the threshold. Default 0.01.

protein_range

residue range for the coverage, as in general_info(). Default: first to last covered residue.

file

optional output file: .csv or .md (markdown table).

states

optional states to include (the first one is the reference). Default: every state.

Value

data frame with columns Item and one per state (invisibly when file is given).

See also

all_summary(), output_prep(), hdx_results_table()

Examples

file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
hdx_summary_table(file_nm, metadata = list(
  "HDX reaction details" = "PBS pD 7.4, 85% D2O, 22 C",
  "Data analysis software" = "HDExaminer 3; HDXBoxeR"))
#>                               Item                                  Unbound
#> 1             HDX reaction details                PBS pD 7.4, 85% D2O, 22 C
#> 2           Data analysis software                   HDExaminer 3; HDXBoxeR

#> 4                     HDX controls undeuterated (0s); fully deuterated (FD)
#> 5             Number of replicates                                        3
#> 6               Number of peptides                                       37
#> 7            Sequence coverage (%)                  94.09 (residues 40-225)
#> 8           Average peptide length                                    13.86
#> 9                       Redundancy                                     2.93
#> 10 Back-exchange (%): mean (range)                     27.01 (1.31 - 51.48)
#> 11   Repeatability (pooled SD, Da)                                    0.067
#> 12  Significant differences in HDX                          reference state
#>                                                                               bound
#> 1                                                         PBS pD 7.4, 85% D2O, 22 C
#> 2                                                            HDExaminer 3; HDXBoxeR
#> 3                                                   3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 4                                          undeuterated (0s); fully deuterated (FD)
#> 5                                                                                 3
#> 6                                                                                34
#> 7                                                           94.09 (residues 40-225)
#> 8                                                                             13.29
#> 9                                                                              2.58
#> 10                                                            35.44 (11.73 - 99.88)
#> 11                                                                            0.076
#> 12 |difference| > 0.20-0.35 Da (critical interval, alpha = 0.01) and Welch p < 0.01
